transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Any time I have to deal with those stronger cleaning chemicals, I either go out of my way to avoid them or push through it while feeling like I can’t stand being there. It has gotten to the point where it's starting to threaten my job, so my union representative suggested I come talk to you.

Do you feel this intense fear or avoidance only when you are in direct contact with the cleaning chemicals, or do you also experience this level of anxiety when you are in crowded public places or situations where escape might be difficult?

No, I don't have any trouble being in crowded places or other situations like that at all. This fear is strictly tied to the cleaning chemicals, their smell, and the storage closets where they're kept. Outside of dealing with those products, I feel completely fine.

Does your fear specifically involve a concern about the potential for physical harm or injury from the chemicals, or is it primarily a reaction to the smell or the physical presence of the substances themselves?

It’s really a combination of both. It started because I was actually overwhelmed by fumes and ended up in the ER two years ago, so I worry about that happening again. But now, it has also become an automatic reaction where my heart races the second I smell them or even see a hazard label, even when I know the cleaner is perfectly safe.

When you encounter these chemicals, is your primary fear that you will have an immediate physical reaction like an allergic response or breathing trouble, or are you more concerned about developing a serious illness or disease from them over time?

It is definitely about having an immediate physical reaction rather than a long-term illness. Ever since that ER visit, my main dread is that I won't be able to breathe, that I'll choke on the fumes, or pass out right on the spot. I just feel this sudden, overwhelming panic that I need to escape immediately.
